claims.text: The starting material is an as-received, coarse-grained CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy.
Friction stir processing can produce an approximately 50 μm-thick surface layer with submicron grains in CoCrFeNi.
Pre-oxidation at 600–700 °C in air will form an oxide scale on the processed CoCrFeNi surface.
The combined processing produces a nanocrystalline surface layer plus a preformed oxide scale.
Surface nanocrystallization enhances the formation and stability of protective oxide tribofilms.
A nanocrystalline oxide glaze or tribofilm can provide tribochemical protection and solid lubrication, leading to gentler wear.
Coarse-grained material is more susceptible to frictional softening, oxide-layer cracking, increased friction, and increased specific wear rate.
The treated CoCrFeNi surface will maintain a coefficient of friction below 0.3 from 25 to 800 °C.
The treated CoCrFeNi surface will have a lower coefficient of friction than untreated coarse-grained CoCrFeNi under identical conditions.
The treated CoCrFeNi surface will have a lower wear rate than untreated coarse-grained CoCrFeNi throughout 25–800 °C.
The treatment will remain effective in air under normal loads from 10 to 100 N.
Performance under more aggressive environments or substantially higher loads is uncertain.
The exact magnitude of the friction and wear reductions is not established and the process may require refinement for extreme conditions.
A controlled comparison can use treated and as-received CoCrFeNi specimens tested in air over 25–800 °C and 10–100 N.
Failure of the treated specimen to retain lower friction or wear than the as-received control would falsify the hypothesis.
